newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan to try alleged coup plotters soon.
newsitem.headline: Sudan to try alleged coup plotters soon.

text.p: Sudan will put on trial a number of people who took part in an alleged plot to attack government targets in Port Sudan with Eritrean help and overthrow President Omar Hassan al-Bashir, the Sudanese defence minister said.

The official Sudan news agency, SUNA, quoted Lieutenant General Hassan Abdel-Rahman Ali as telling the National Assembly (parliament) on Monday that Eritrean troops were set to help opposition party members with the takeover of the port.

Ali did not say how many people would stand trial, but SUNA reported in August that no more than 25 people had been arrested, including 17 military men, in connection with the plot to attack vital installations in the Red Sea port and disrupt Sudan's foreign trade.
Officials at the time said the majority of those summoned for interrogation had been released after questioning.
The Sudanese opposition Democratic Unionist Party, based in Cairo, said in August the army had executed 11 military officers on charges of taking part in the alleged conspiracy.
The party said Sudanese authorities fabricated the conspiracy story to cover up a purge of army officers hostile to Bashir and that 56 people remained in detention in Port Sudan.
The army denied the reports. Ali told parliament the reports were "baseless and unfounded".

He said the plotters had recuited two retired officers in Port Sudan, 15 serving officers and three non-commissioned officers. The plotters had instructed the army men to occupy the port and sieze vital establishments.

Ali said the detainees told investigators that three Eritrean ships carrying mercenaries and ammunition as well as a "foreign intervention force" that was to arrive through the airport were to support their occupation of Port Sudan.

"After occupying Port Sudan, the so-called National Alliance forces and Eritrean troops planned to seize Kassala area, declare a state and carry out assassination operations in the eastern area," Ali said.
Eritrea supports opposition groups fighting to oust Khartoum's Islamist-backed government which it says is destablising the region.
A number of Sudanese parliamentarians said their country should support Eritrean rebels in retaliation for Asmara's cooperation, but Ali did not comment.
